H1732.name: David
H1732.desc: King living at the time of United Monarchy
H1732.brief: Anointed king of Israel, ancestor of Jesus Christ
H1732.short: David, son of Jesse, was the anointed king of Israel, a man after God's own heart, and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.

H1719B.name: Dedan
H1719B.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1719B.brief: Grandson of Cush, son of Raamah
H1719B.short: Dedan was a grandson of Cush and a son of Raamah.

H1719C.name: Dedan
H1719C.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1719C.short: Dedan was a grandson of Abraham through Jokshan, born to Keturah.

H1723.name: Dehavites
H1723.desc: Word sometimes translated as a name
H1723.brief: People group who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem
H1723.short: The Dehavites were a people group who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem during the time of Ezra.

H1704.name: Dibri
H1704.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1704.brief: Father of Shelomith, whose son blasphemed God's name
H1704.short: Dibri, of the tribe of Dan, was the father of Shelomith, whose son blasphemed the name of God and was stoned to death.

H1783.name: Dinah
H1783.desc: Jacob's daughter living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1783.short: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, was raped by Shechem, leading to a violent confrontation between her brothers and the Shechemites.

H1784.name: Dinaites
H1784.desc: Word sometimes translated as a name
H1784.brief: People group who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem
H1784.short: The Dinaites were one of the groups who wrote to King Artaxerxes, opposing the rebuilding of Jerusalem during Ezra's time.

H1789G.name: Dishan
H1789G.desc: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1789G.short: Dishan was a descendant of Seir the Horite, mentioned in the genealogies of Esau's family.

H1787G.name: Dishon
H1787G.desc: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1787G.brief: Descendant of Seir the Horite, son of Anah
H1787G.short: Dishon was a descendant of Seir the Horite and the son of Anah, mentioned in the genealogies of Esau's family.

H1787H.name: Dishon
H1787H.desc: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1787H.brief: Grandson of Seir the Horite through Anah
H1787H.short: Dishon was a grandson of Seir the Horite through Anah, mentioned in the genealogies of Esau's family.

H1721.name: Dodanim
H1721.brief: Descendants of Javan, son of Japheth
H1721.short: The Dodanim were descendants of Javan, son of Japheth, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

H1735.name: Dodavahu
H1735.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1735.brief: Prophet who rebuked Jehoshaphat for his alliance with Ahaziah
H1735.short: Dodavahu, son of Eliezer of Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat for his alliance with Ahaziah, king of Israel.

H1734I.name: Dodo
H1734I.desc: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
H1734I.brief: Father of Elhanan, one of David's mighty men
H1734I.short: Dodo the Bethlehemite was the father of Elhanan, one of David's mighty men.

H1734H.name: Dodo
H1734H.desc: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
H1734H.brief: Father of Eleazar, one of David's mighty men
H1734H.short: Dodo, also known as Dodai, was the father of Eleazar, one of David's mighty men who fought valiantly in battle.

H1734G.name: Dodo
H1734G.brief: Son of Puah, a judge of Israel
H1734G.short: Dodo, son of Puah, was a judge of Israel who led the nation for 23 years.

H1746G.name: Dumah
H1746G.desc: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1746G.brief: Son of Ishmael and grandson of Abraham
H1746G.short: Dumah was a son of Ishmael and grandson of Abraham, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and Chronicles.

H1708.name: Dabbesheth
H1708.short: Dabbesheth was a town on the border of the territory allocated to the tribe of Zebulun.

H1705.name: Daberath
H1705.short: Daberath was a Levitical city located in the territory of Issachar, later given to the Levites of the Gershonite clan.

H1719A.name: Dedan
H1719A.brief: An Arabian people and region, involved in trade.
H1719A.short: Dedan was an Arabian people and region, known for their involvement in trade.

H1769H.name: Dibon
H1769H.brief: A city in Judah, inhabited by the tribe of Judah.
H1769H.short: Dibon, a city in Judah, was inhabited by the tribe of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:25">Nehemiah 11:25</ref>).

H1769G.name: Dibon
H1769G.brief: Moabite city, allotted to Gad, later possessed by Moab.
H1769G.short: Dibon, also known as Dibon-gad, was a Moabite city allotted to the tribe of Gad, later repossessed by Moab.

H1776.name: Dimonah
H1776.brief: A city in the Negev region of Judah.
H1776.short: Dimonah, a city located in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:22">Joshua 15:22</ref>).

H1774.name: Dizahab
H1774.brief: A place near where Moses delivered his final speeches.
H1774.short: Dizahab, a place near where Moses delivered his final speeches to the Israelites (<ref="Deu.1.1">Deu.1.1</ref>).

H1756G.name: Dor
H1756G.brief: A Canaanite city, later allotted to Manasseh but not conquered.
H1756G.short: Dor, also known as Naphath-dor, was a Canaanite city allotted to Manasseh but not fully conquered (<ref="Joshua 12:23; 17:11; Judges 1:27">Joshua 12:23; 17:11; Judges 1:27</ref>).

H1746H.name: Dumah
H1746H.brief: A city or region in Arabia, recipient of a prophetic oracle.
H1746H.short: Dumah, a city or region in Arabia, was the recipient of a prophetic oracle in <ref="Isaiah 21:11">Isaiah 21:11</ref>.

H1757.name: Dura
H1757.brief: A plain in Babylon where Nebuchadnezzar set up a statue.
H1757.short: Dura, a plain in the province of Babylon where King Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden statue (<ref="Dan.3.1">Dan.3.1</ref>).

H1709G.name: Fish Gate
H1709G.brief: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time
H1709G.short: The Fish Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time and was a location of judgment and trade.

H1712.name: Dagon
H1712.brief: Philistine god whose temple was destroyed by Samson
H1712.short: Dagon was the chief deity of the Philistines, with temples at Gaza and Ashdod.
